name: Leidos Holdings, Inc.
reason: Solid 15% adj EPS CAGR but EBIT margin 12.2% is a 10y high vs 8.5% avg (EPS 1.0x 10y max) and earnings hinge on federal budget/contract recompete decisions that are hard to forecast 5-10 years out.

name: PHINIA, Inc.
reason: 2023 spin-off making fuel-injection systems for combustion engines faces EV substitution; ROIC ~5% and EPS 0.58x of its short peak - cheap but not special.

name: Lear Corp.
reason: Auto seating/wiring supplier with EBIT margin collapsed from 8.5% to 4.4% and 10y EPS CAGR of 1.7%; customer-dictated pricing in a cyclical industry leaves no specialness.

name: Virtus Investment Partners, Inc.
reason: Active asset manager whose earnings track market levels and fund flows (EPS fell from 35.92 in 2021 to 25.06; consensus FY1 -10.9%) with secular pressure from passive.

name: The Bank of New York Mellon Corp.
reason: Custody/clearing oligopoly with sticky fee-based relationships, 8/10 years of >=7% EPS growth, falling share count (-4.3%/yr) and consensus 11-12% EPS growth; watch NII rate sensitivity with EPS at 10y high.

name: Gartner, Inc.
reason: Historically great subscription research franchise (ROIC ~17%, FCF conversion 1.5x) but EPS fell to 13.17 in 2025 and AI-driven disintermediation of seat-based research is a credible 5-year threat.

name: Owens Corning
reason: Roofing/insulation earnings tied to housing and repair cycles (EPS down 24% in 2025 from a 2024 peak, consensus FY1 -20%) and growth increasingly acquired (acq/FCF 0.63, Masonite).

name: Precigen, Inc.
reason: Loss-making synthetic biology/gene therapy biotech with negative EPS every year since 2015 and binary clinical/regulatory outcomes.

name: Ameresco, Inc.
reason: Energy-efficiency/renewables contractor with net debt/EBITDA 7.7x, negative cumulative FCF and EPS at 0.48x its 2022 peak - balance sheet fails a recession test.

name: Adient plc
reason: Auto seating supplier with ~3% EBIT margin, negative 10y average ROIC and EPS at 0.2x of 2017 level; commodity-like supplier economics.

name: Orchid Island Capital, Inc.
reason: Levered agency RMBS mortgage REIT whose earnings are set by rate spreads (net debt/EBITDA 20x, share count +41%/yr, EPS 0.11x 10y max).

name: Corpay, Inc.
reason: Scaled fleet-card and B2B payments network with ~45% EBIT margins, 13% 10y adj EPS CAGR, net debt/EBITDA 0.45x and consensus 15-18% growth; caveat that acquisitions (acq/FCF 0.59) and fuel prices contribute to growth.

name: NRG Energy, Inc.
reason: Competitive power generator/retailer exposed to wholesale power and gas prices, with acquisition-led growth (acq/FCF 1.22: Vivint, LS Power assets) and net debt/EBITDA 3.2x.

name: Verra Mobility Corp.
reason: Toll/red-light-camera services with good margins (24.6%) but heavy acquisition history (acq/FCF 1.1), 2.8x leverage, rental-car/municipal contract concentration, and a $2.81 price at 2.9x NTM EPS signals a severe dislocation or data issue to verify.

name: Virtu Financial, Inc.
reason: Market-making earnings driven by trading volumes and volatility (EPS 5.76 in 2020 to 1.84 in 2023 to 5.73 in 2025) - capital-markets activity no one can forecast.

name: First Hawaiian, Inc.
reason: Conservative Hawaii bank but essentially no growth (EPS 2.20 in 2025 vs 2.19 in 2019, 3/9 years >=7%) - ordinary bank without a route to 7% EPS growth.

name: Pinnacle Financial Partners, Inc.
reason: Strong organic growth record (12.8% EPS CAGR) but the 2025 merger of equals with Synovus is a recent transformation that makes the combined bank's 5-10 year economics hard to forecast.

name: CDW Corp.
reason: Well-run IT reseller (ROIC ~14%, EPS 1.0x 10y max) but a low-margin (7.4%) distribution business with 2.8x net debt/EBITDA and EPS flat since 2022 - good but not special.

name: Preferred Bank (California)
reason: High-ROE (17%) commercial bank but earnings ride the rate cycle with EPS 0.99x of 10y peak, CRE concentration, and consensus growth only 3-4% for FY1/FY2.

name: ANI Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
reason: Generics plus Cortrophin Gel roll-up with acquisitions 2.0x cumulative FCF, negative 10y ROIC, a 268% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap and single-product rare-disease concentration.
